title: Relational databases
description: The replacement relational collection, in draft.

entries.title: Relational databases
entries.brief: Understand shared relational facts, questions and guarded changes through one shop purchase. Distinguish schema rules, atomicity, concurrent decisions, query work and durability, judge relational fit and choose a practical next route.

entries.title: Relational data modelling
entries.brief: Design rows, keys and relationships that express the shop’s facts accurately. Diagnose dependencies and redundancy, distinguish historical facts from derived copies, and judge normalisation and modelling variations through required changes.

entries.title: Normalisation and decomposition
entries.brief: Derive candidate keys from declared dependencies and choose lossless, dependency-preserving decompositions where possible. Own closure, synthesis, 3NF versus BCNF, multivalued and join dependencies, and higher normal forms. The parent develops practical diagnoses and simple reconstruction examples.

entries.title: Modelling hierarchies
entries.brief: Choose and maintain trees or shared ancestry with adjacency lists, edge tables, paths, closure tables and nested sets. Compare traversal, reparenting, cycle prevention and consistency costs; the parent introduces recursive references and the tree-versus-multiple-parents decision.

entries.title: Values, missing data and equality
entries.brief: Choose money, time, text and identity representations from their meanings. Reason about conversion, precision, collation, equality, ordering and NULL, including three-valued predicates and uniqueness edge cases.

entries.title: Constraints and data integrity
entries.brief: Express identity, required values, row checks, references and exclusions in enforceable schema rules. Preserve tenant integrity with composite identities and references, and distinguish declarative enforcement, triggers and invariants needing a concurrency protocol.

entries.title: History, correction and deletion
entries.brief: Represent agreements and changing facts with explicit effective and recorded times. Carry corrections, retention and deletion through related and external records without rewriting the meaning of historical purchases.

entries.title: Joins and the meaning of a result row
entries.brief: Build SELECT and JOIN results with deliberate row meaning. Predict multiplicity and missing matches, use existence tests, distinguish compatible-row set operations and their duplicates from joining columns, and complete the still-due report by summarising lines and payments separately per order.

entries.title: Aggregates and window functions
entries.brief: Choose grouped or per-row calculations without losing the intended grain. Own general GROUP BY, HAVING, FILTER, empty inputs and counts, deterministic ordering, ranking, peers and window frames.

entries.title: Pagination and consistent exports
entries.brief: Choose a continuation contract for a changing list and a snapshot contract for an export. Build keyset cursors that preserve ties and explain omissions, duplicates, retention and cancellation costs.

entries.title: Updates, upserts and bulk imports
entries.brief: Make changes conditional and interpret affected rows. Choose conflict meaning for an upsert and stage, validate and reconcile replayable batches, including a rejected row and a partially processed import.

entries.title: SQL at the application boundary
entries.brief: Preserve query meaning and transaction ownership across drivers, pools and ORMs. Separate parameters from SQL structure, map results, bound repeated queries, and handle one request’s connection, error and cancellation coherently.

entries.title: Transactions and isolation
entries.brief: Choose atomic work and isolation from the invariant being preserved. Distinguish committed visibility, statement and transaction snapshots and serial outcomes; develop sound one-row stock and multi-row capacity protocols.

entries.title: Locks, contention and deadlocks
entries.brief: Choose a lockable authority and a sound isolation and snapshot protocol for a decision. Design lock scope and acquisition order, then diagnose deadlocks and bound waiting without weakening the invariant.

entries.title: Retries and uncertain commit outcomes
entries.brief: Distinguish a known abort from a commit whose reply was lost. Reuse one logical request identity, reject conflicting payloads, and recover the recorded result rather than applying a purchase twice.

entries.title: Outboxes and database-backed jobs
entries.brief: Commit a durable intention with the domain change, then deliver or claim work despite duplicate execution and worker loss. Design deduplication, leases, expiry and fencing so recovery preserves the intended external effects.

entries.title: Query execution and performance
entries.brief: Follow rows through scans, joins, grouping and sorting. Use measured plans to locate bad cardinality estimates, repeated work, spills and data movement; test a repair against realistic parameters and workload.

entries.title: Indexes and access paths
entries.brief: Derive useful index keys, ranges, ordering and covering from a query and the distribution of values. Compare pages and rows examined with rows returned, then weigh write, space and maintenance costs across the workload.

entries.title: Table partitioning and data lifecycle
entries.brief: Choose a partition boundary for useful pruning or retention without assuming it distributes work across servers. Derive pruning from predicates and account for global identity, references and safe partition retirement.

entries.title: Storage and durability
entries.brief: Connect logical updates to pages, buffers, retained row versions and cleanup, distinguishing reusable space, file shrinkage and write amplification. Explain write-ahead ordering, commit durability and restart recovery, and separate them from recovery after lost storage or an unwanted committed change.

entries.title: Backup, restore and reconciliation
entries.brief: Choose and verify a restorable history from recovery-point and recovery-time needs. Test the backup chain and restore target, close the source history, and reconcile valid later work and external effects without duplicate application.

entries.title: Replicas, lag and read routing
entries.brief: Trace copied history through received, durable and replayed progress. Choose read routing from freshness and failure promises, including read-your-write needs, stale reads and log retention.

entries.title: Failover and fencing
entries.brief: Distinguish suspected failure from authority to write. Fence a former writer, choose a promotion point with an explicit loss boundary, reconcile divergence and rejoin safely.

entries.title: Diagnosing a database incident
entries.brief: Start with a slow or failing request and use evidence to distinguish pool delay, lock waits, expensive execution and storage pressure. Choose a bounded intervention and account for its recovery cost.

entries.title: Live schema changes and backfills
entries.brief: Move through compatible schema and caller states using expand, migrate and contract. Prove a backfill converged despite races and late rows, and define acceptance and return boundaries.

entries.title: Connections, overload and capacity
entries.brief: Distinguish connections, active work and queued requests, then budget admitted work and recovery headroom around the real limiting resource. Choose bounded overload behaviour and validate capacity under a representative workload.

entries.title: Database access and least privilege
entries.brief: Derive runtime, migration and support privileges from their tasks. Test tenant access as the actual trusted identity, distinguishing database authorisation, application identity and row-level integrity.

entries.title: Sharding and distributed SQL
entries.brief: Choose a distribution boundary from local work, invariant scope and the actual bottleneck. Distinguish replicas from shards, explain authoritative replicated history, acknowledgements and quorum availability, and separate agreement within one partition from atomic commit across partitions. Derive locality, skew, fan-out and coordination from the key.

entries.title: Transactions across partitions
entries.brief: Explain atomic outcomes across partitions, including recovery of a distributed decision after coordinator loss. Distinguish replica agreement from transaction commit and connect invariant scope to the participants that must coordinate.

entries.title: Time, snapshots and distributed reads
entries.brief: Read related partitions at a safe common history. Compare logical timestamps, clock uncertainty and safe historical reads while distinguishing a past observation from authority for a current decision.

entries.title: Regional placement and survival
entries.brief: Place data and voting replicas against stated latency and survival needs. Derive quorum survival from failure domains and trace the remote coordination introduced by apparently local data and global invariants.

entries.title: Rebalancing and cluster change
entries.brief: Move replicas and data while preserving authoritative history. Explain catch-up and safe membership change, and budget rebalancing and decommissioning without treating lost redundancy as spare capacity.

entries.title: Inside PostgreSQL
entries.brief: Trace one connection and request through PostgreSQL processes, shared buffers, heap tuples and indexes. Explain tuple visibility, HOT updates and their physical limits so native plans and maintenance have a concrete physical setting.

entries.title: PostgreSQL vacuum and transaction age
entries.brief: Diagnose retained PostgreSQL versions, visibility and transaction-age risk before changing maintenance. Distinguish reusable space from bloat and file shrinkage; choose vacuum and related interventions from retained horizons and age evidence.

entries.title: PostgreSQL index methods and operators
entries.brief: Choose a PostgreSQL access method and operator class from the operator’s meaning and data organisation. Compare B-tree, hash, GIN, GiST, SP-GiST and BRIN, and verify candidates, rechecks and write costs in native plans.

entries.title: Reading and repairing PostgreSQL plans
entries.brief: Interpret EXPLAIN ANALYZE counters without confusing estimates, per-loop work, buffers or timings. Test statistics, access paths and prepared-plan repairs under skew and workload variation.

entries.title: PostgreSQL JSON and structured alternatives
entries.brief: Choose columns, related rows or JSONB from the facts, validation and update boundary. Match native JSON operators and indexes while preserving established identities, types and data rules.

entries.title: PostgreSQL WAL, checkpoints and durability
entries.brief: Interpret PostgreSQL WAL progress, checkpoint work and commit settings against a tested durability promise. Explain an isolated crash drill and its restart evidence without extrapolating to power loss or lost storage.

entries.title: Restoring PostgreSQL to a recovery target
entries.brief: Build and test a base-backup and archived-WAL chain, restore a verified target and account for valid work outside the recovered history. Close source writes before reconciliation and preserve external-effect identity.

entries.title: PostgreSQL physical replicas and promotion
entries.brief: Operate a physical standby with separate receipt, flush and replay evidence. Choose synchronous promises, perform fenced promotion with an explicit loss boundary, and return a former primary safely.

entries.title: PostgreSQL logical replication and change feeds
entries.brief: Configure a publication and subscriber with deliberate replica identity. Treat the stream as selective row changes, accounting for schema, sequences, lag, retained log and cutover responsibilities.

entries.title: PostgreSQL schema changes under load
entries.brief: Choose native schema and index operations from their lock, rewrite and validity behaviour. Bound waits, validate backfill convergence and maintain indexes without accepting incomplete semantic or physical work.

entries.title: Operating and diagnosing PostgreSQL
entries.brief: Trace a request through pool and server evidence to distinguish blocked work, excessive execution and connection pressure. Test a targeted intervention with bounded waits and account for recovery costs.

entries.title: PostgreSQL roles, policies and privileged code
entries.brief: Test role inheritance, ownership and row-policy boundaries as the actual application identities. Explain bypass cases and secure privileged routines against identity and name-resolution mistakes.

entries.title: Upgrading and migrating PostgreSQL
entries.brief: Choose between a major upgrade and a logical migration, then rehearse compatibility, a recoverable write handover and acceptance. Identify the point after which a simple return is no longer possible.

entries.title: Distributing PostgreSQL work
entries.brief: Choose among native partitions, application shards, Citus and foreign tables from co-location, invariant scope and movement needs. Derive local work, skew and fan-out, then preserve single ownership through a transfer.

entries.title: Full-text search in PostgreSQL
entries.brief: Build text retrieval from tokens, phrases and configuration through ranked, filtered results. Keep indexed candidate retrieval, linguistic matching and relevance evaluation distinct, including maintenance when source text or configuration changes.

entries.title: Vector search in PostgreSQL
entries.brief: Evaluate vector retrieval independently from the embedding model’s semantic usefulness. Compare exact, HNSW and IVFFlat retrieval under filtering, nearest-neighbour recall, latency and index lifecycle costs.

entries.title: Types and extensions in PostgreSQL
entries.brief: Express overlap and spatial predicates with suitable types, operators and indexes. Own extension installation, privileges, dependencies, restore, upgrade and removal, including when an extension becomes part of the application’s durability contract.

entries.title: Inside CockroachDB
entries.brief: Trace SQL data through ordered keys, ranges, local storage and replicated ownership. Explain splits, leases and replica agreement with enough detail to see why a hotspot can persist as a cluster grows.

entries.title: CockroachDB transactions and retries
entries.brief: Relate intents and transaction state to atomic visibility, then handle native transaction retry and ambiguous-result paths for one logical purchase. Preserve the request identity and keep external work outside a replayed transaction.

entries.title: CockroachDB isolation and follower reads
entries.brief: Choose Serializable, Read Committed and historical reads from the decision they must support. Explain safe follower reads, freshness and retention limits without treating a historical observation as current authority.

entries.title: CockroachDB query work and hot ranges
entries.brief: Locate lookups, fan-out, SQL/KV work, network movement and contention from native evidence. Weigh covering and distributed keys against write and ordering costs, and separate less work from a hot-key bottleneck.

entries.title: CockroachDB table locality and region survival
entries.brief: Choose regional-by-table, regional-by-row or GLOBAL tables and survival goals from actual access and failure requirements. Verify placement and survival, and distinguish structural reasoning from measured regional latency.

entries.title: Operating and securing a CockroachDB cluster
entries.brief: Verify secure runtime identity, least privilege and tenant isolation. Use native evidence to diagnose under-replication and range health, then remove a node without consuming the cluster’s survival budget.

entries.title: CockroachDB backup and recovery
entries.brief: Validate full and incremental backup coverage and restore scope. Restore the intended history, close source writes, and reconcile a later valid booking by identity, capacity and external effects without consuming capacity twice.

entries.title: CockroachDB schema jobs under load
entries.brief: Treat schema changes as observable jobs inside an application compatibility protocol. Interpret progress, failure and cleanup, and accept a backfill or unique index only after semantic checks.

entries.title: Upgrading a CockroachDB cluster
entries.brief: Rehearse binary rollout and the cluster-version boundary. Distinguish mixed binaries from finalised compatibility, and verify application acceptance, rollback eligibility and recovery choices.

entries.title: Moving a SQL application to CockroachDB
entries.brief: Find semantic incompatibilities behind similar SQL, then port the application contract. Validate a consistent copy, transfer one write authority and reconcile a return path with explicit limits once new writes are accepted.
